info.description: For developers: agent manifests, Agents, sessions (with AG-UI and A2A) and artifacts, through `@nylorun/agents`. Every Tenant serves it on its one URL, beside the Management API (`/openapi/management.json`). Every request sends `Nylorun-Protocol`. Who may call each operation is its `security` and its `x-nylorun-credentials` and `x-nylorun-scopes` (the subject scopes that reach it) fields: an application key (servers) or a trusted issuer's token (browsers and apps).

servers.description: A Runtime: a local Tenant (`nylorun start`), or where yours runs

applicationKey.description: An application key of the Tenant (`PUT /v1/tenant/keys/{keyId}`), or Studio's key, derived from the admin key. With `Nylorun-Subject` and `Nylorun-Scopes`, it acts for that person, narrowed to those scopes. Never accepted from a browser (`Origin`).

managementKey.description: A management key of the Tenant (role `management`): it reaches the Management API (`/v1/tenant/*`) and `/v1/me`, as itself, never for a subject. Issued only on the Tenant's machine (`nylorun-operate keys put <id> --role management`) or from `NYLORUN_MANAGEMENT_KEY_FILE`. Never accepted from a browser (`Origin`).

issuerToken.description: A JWT from a trusted issuer of the Host's identity file (Host feature `trusted-issuers`): one person, with the issuer's scopes, agents and sandbox grants, until it expires. Accepted from servers and browsers alike; CORS is the operator's proxy's.

put.description: Saves the manifest as its next version, or answers the latest unchanged when nothing differs. Every Agent that tracks the manifest moves to the new version (track T3): at once, at its pod's next start for a runtime change a pod applies only when it starts, or once a required secret the version adds is set; a pinned one stays, and so does one whose kind, harness or storage the version changes (`agents_behind`). The Runtime checks the harness and runtime sections against each other: a custom harness needs a pod with an image, every credential the harness names is a declared slot of the right type, and the runtime's kind gives the loop the sandbox it needs; every gap is named in one `422 manifest_inconsistent` (`details.gaps`). `If-Match: <version>` refuses the save with `412 manifest_changed` when the latest version is no longer the one you read (`0` for a manifest that does not exist yet). With `?dryRun=true` the answer is the plan: the changes by section, every reason a save would be refused (`errors`, the gaps first), warnings, the Agents it would move (`moves`) and how many stay on older versions (`behind`); nothing is saved. Clients compose the authoring files and drop their `$schema` before they send one document.

put.summary: Create, find or move an Agent
put.description: Creates the Agent, its vault and its compute from a saved agent manifest, within the Tenant's limits, or answers the one with this id, so get-or-create is one call. `manifest: "name"` records that it tracks the manifest (its latest version, and each version saved later) and `"name@n"` that it is pinned; the version it runs is `resolvedVersion`. On an existing one, labels replace, `owner` sets or (with `null`) clears the owner guard, and `manifest` moves it (track T3) with its id, disk, vault and sessions: a harness-only change applies at once (each session's next turn runs it), a runtime change of a pod at its next start (`targetVersion`, `waitingFor: start`), and a version that adds a required secret once a value is set (`waitingFor: secrets`). Its manifest's name, kind, harness and storage are fixed (`409 agent_fixed_field`): fork it to change them. `?dryRun=true` answers the move's plan and changes nothing. Creating an Agent opens no session (D71). Kind `pod` needs sandbox pods (`nylorun local sandbox enable`) and is created at once.

tags.name: Agent manifests
tags.description: Named, versioned agent manifests (protocol 16): one document with what runs inside an agent's loop (`harness`) and what the Runtime provides around it (`runtime`), checked against each other when it is saved. Save one with a plan first (`?dryRun=true`) and `If-Match`; an Agent is made from one version and keeps it, so a save changes no Agent. `client.agentManifests` in `@nylorun/agents`, and `nylorun apply`.

tags.name: Definition files
tags.description: The files an agent manifest names by the SHA-256 of their bytes (each skill's folder, a runtime section's input files): upload each once before saving the manifest, which is refused while it names one the Runtime does not hold (`definition_files_missing`) or a skill whose files hold more than its skill limit together (`limit_exceeded`; `/v1/tenant/skills`, default 2 GiB). No file and no count of files has a limit of its own. `client.agentManifests.save` in `@nylorun/agents` does both.

tags.name: Agents
tags.description: The live instances of agent manifests: an Agent has a stable id, its manifest version, one sandbox (a virtual workspace, a pod with its own volume, or none), one vault of secrets for its shell, MCP servers and HTTP tools, its disk versions, and its sessions. Its `state` says whether it is working, sleeping, needs a person (`input_required`), is failing or paused. Create or find one from a saved manifest, watch its lifecycle, stop, reset, fork or delete it, and write its secrets. In `@nylorun/agents`.

tags.name: Triggers
tags.description: What starts an Agent's turns with no client connected (track T4, D74): the schedules, one-shot times and webhook endpoints its manifest's `runtime.triggers` declare. Each trigger's status is the Agent's: pause and resume it, run it now, make a webhook trigger's signing secret, and read its runs (`started`, `queued`, `skipped` or `failed`, with a reason). In `@nylorun/agents` and `nylorun agents triggers`.

tags.name: Sessions API
tags.description: A conversation with an Agent: open a session on it, send commands, follow its events, read its history. No session is special: an app that keeps one conversation going reuses its id. In `@nylorun/agents`.

tags.name: AG-UI
tags.description: The same sessions through AG-UI: a thread is one session per person, Agent and thread, and each run is a turn.

tags.name: A2A
tags.description: The same sessions through Agent2Agent: a context is one session per subject, Agent and `contextId`, and a task is one turn; every caller's session runs on the Agent's disk and vault, so an app that serves several audiences makes an Agent for each. The card is how an A2A client finds the Agent.

tags.name: Artifacts
tags.description: Files and folders agents and people produce, versioned, with short-lived capability links to share them. In `@nylorun/agents`.

tags.name: Service
tags.description: Check a Runtime is up and speaks your protocol, ask who your credential is, find the identity providers it takes tokens from, and read the public keys of the tokens it signs. `/health`, `/ready`, the protected resource metadata, the JWKS and the documents need no key.
